### Investment Memo: NXT (Nextpower Inc., f/k/a Nextracker) — 3 November 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD — Initiate small for unexposed portfolios | Conviction: **Medium**
**Price Target**: $95 (~4% upside from $91.13) | Probability-weighted range: $62 bear / $90 base / $125 bull
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

---

**Investment Thesis**

NXT is the undisputed leader in utility-scale solar trackers (revenue 2.8x its nearest pure-play rival, >$6B backlog, record bookings, seven consecutive beats averaging +17.8%) with a fortress balance sheet (~$1.0B net cash, zero long-term debt) — but it is a good business trading *at* intrinsic value, not below it. Value's DCF base sits at ~$88 against a $91 spot price, FCF has been flat at ~$500M for three years while revenue grew 42%, and three independent agents converged on the same finding: **~31–40% of gross profit is policy-contingent (45X credits + tariff recoveries) while gross margin has fallen four consecutive quarters (35.9% → 31.1%)**. The 51% de-rating from May to October has already absorbed most of the hostile macro (10Y 5.13%, real yield 2.60%), so this is a stock where the *price*, not the *franchise*, is the debate — and the Nov-16 Capital Markets Day is the swing factor.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector structurally attractive (~20% tracker volume CAGR, oligopoly, new non-subsidy demand driver in data-centre load growth; ~216–240 GW safe-harboured pipeline converts to contracted demand through CY2027). Macro is the headwind: a re-hiking Fed, bear-steepening long end, construction PPI +11%, copper +45% — hostile to the *multiple*, not the *earnings*, and the multiple has already compressed ~42%. NXT converts margin better than any peer save FSLR (19.6% op margin vs 11.9% peer median on a *below*-median gross margin) — the signature of real operating leverage.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **MEDIUM risk, and the binding sizing constraint.** 77–83% US revenue; 45X credits of ~$103M/quarter (~31% of gross profit) plus a $312M receivable rest on FEOC content thresholds tightening from 50% (2026) to 85% (2030). Section 232 steel/tariff churn is a recurring margin event. Legal risk has *improved* (securities class action dismissed March 2026); GameChange patent war is two-way and non-existential. Downgrade trigger: any 45X disallowance or adverse FEOC interpretation.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: HOLD, do not initiate at $91. Narrow (but real) moat; ROIC 29.2% but decaying from 50.6% two years ago; DCF $76–102, base ~$88. FCF yield 3.6%; FY27 GAAP earnings guided flat-to-down on 56% opex growth. No margin of safety — the price already embeds a decade of high-teens FCF growth. Aggressive-buy level: ≤$68.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: BUY. FY27 guide raised twice to $4.2–4.45B (+18–25%), adj EPS $4.61–4.87, PEG ~0.9; at 19x forward adjusted EPS the market implies ~zero growth past FY27 against a backlog of ~1.4x revenue. Storage/BESS ($35B ex-China TAM by 2030; 1.3 GW firm data-centre contracts), power conversion (>2 GW backlog) and 68-country distribution are the bridge over the 2028 policy cliff. Honest caveats: Rule-of-40 of 35, a ~10% Q3 growth guide, policy-contingent EBITDA.
- **Quantitative Signals**: SELL, weak conviction — discounted heavily. Composite 31/100 on 12-1 momentum of −17%, beta 2.65, vol 69%, and eight consecutive Street PT cuts. But the alpha is not statistically distinguishable from zero (t ≈ −0.5), the earnings-revision score is a period-mismatch artifact, and 65–75% of variance is idiosyncratic. The only above-median factor is Quality (65) — which is itself decelerating.
- **Financial Risk**: MODERATE, cleanly bifurcated. Solvency/liquidity risk **LOW** (net cash −1.4x EBITDA, 265x interest coverage, current ratio 2.45, survives a −35% revenue shock with no financing action). Equity risk **HIGH** (69% vol, 51% max drawdown). The scenario that matters is a 500bp gross-margin shock (−$178M EBIT, −26%) — *margin*, not volume, is what you underwrite.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: MODERATE with a High policy overlay. 21 insider sales / 0 buys in six months (incl. a ~$55M director sale and the new CFO selling) — real but bounded by RSU/10b5-1 mechanics and a $162M Q2 buyback. Dual-class controlled-company structure, key-man dependence on Shugar, four-front M&A integration load, bill-and-hold revenue recognition flagged for monitoring.
- **ESG**: NEUTRAL, unusually split. Environmental management is genuinely best-in-class for a small-cap industrial (SBTi-validated targets, assured Scope 1–3, EAF steel) — a *commercial asset* in hyperscaler procurement. Governance scores 4/10 (controlled company, dual class, recent class action) and justifies a persistent valuation discount.
- **Alternative Data**: BULLISH. Consensus Q3 estimate ($1,062M) sits *below* the implied guidance run-rate (~$1.14B/quarter); news flow was positive for two quarters while the stock fell 51% — the Nov-2 +14.9% gap on 2.7x volume looks like the first reconciliation of that decoupling. Rebrand contaminates search data; patent and web-traffic tools failed (gap).
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **NO EDGE — explicitly rejects shorting.** Found genuine earnings-quality erosion (cash conversion through 1.0x, negative operating leverage, goodwill now 33% of equity) but no fraud: Beneish clean, inventory days falling, OCF reconciles. One unresolved item: fiscal-year-end receivables fell ~$780M while working capital moved only +$7.3M — a transparency question, not a manipulation finding. Poor short asymmetry at 16x forward with net cash after a 42% drawdown.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Backlog and bookings are accelerating, not decelerating**: >$6B contracted backlog (~1.4x FY27 revenue) with record bookings and a 100% beat rate; consensus estimates sit below the implied guidance run-rate, setting up a continued upward revision cycle.
- **The platform expansion is already in the numbers**: storage/eBOS/power conversion ~22% of Q2 revenue from near zero two years ago; 1.3 GW of firm AI/hyperscaler data-centre contracts are underwritten on power-scarcity economics, not tax credits — a genuinely durable post-2027 demand driver.
- **The de-rating has done its work**: −51% peak-to-trough on rising estimates; a 10Y retreat to ~4.50% with the current backlog re-rates NXT toward 25x → $120–130.

**Bear Case**
- **Policy-contingent earnings + margin decay**: ~31–40% of gross profit from 45X/tariff recoveries subject to FEOC tightening and clawback risk; gross margin down four straight quarters and guided to the high-20s for H2 FY27 — if 30% breaks, intrinsic value falls ~15–20%.
- **The 2028 air pocket is real**: OBBBA's 31-Dec-2027 placed-in-service deadline pulls demand forward; Q3's ~10% growth guide shows the shape of it, and the BESS/data-centre bridge is unproven at scale.
- **Macro tail-risk compounds**: a December hike taking the 10Y through 5.50% (real >2.90%) defers 2028 COD project FIDs, slows backlog conversion, and compresses the multiple on *falling* FY28 estimates → $60–65.

**Key Risks**
1. **45X/FEOC adverse interpretation or disallowance** — hits volume, margin and multiple simultaneously; the single binding risk (Geo Legal).
2. **Gross margin <30% for two consecutive quarters** — the primary kill-switch; more damaging than a 20% revenue decline (Fin Risk and Short independently converged here).
3. **FY28 demand cliff** if the storage/international bridge underdelivers; backlog falling below $5B invalidates the visibility thesis.
4. **Receivables year-end anomaly** — unresolved pending the IR question on factoring/reclassification; an evasive answer is an escalation trigger.
5. **Rate shock redux** — 10Y >5.50% with real >2.90%; beta 2.65–3.10 means a 20% market drawdown ≈ 35–40% NXT drawdown.

**Portfolio Construction Note** (from Portfolio Strategist)

**Initiate 1.0% — scaled, not bought.** Twelve of twelve agents agree the franchise and balance sheet are real; the disagreement is purely about entry price, and a probability-weighted ~3.4% edge against 69% volatility is a coin flip — Kelly math says starter, not position. Size it as a **2.65% beta instrument, not a 1% allocation**.

- **Execution in thirds**: 0.5% now (~$91) / 0.5% at $76–80 (gap fill + late-Oct low) / 1.0% only post-CMD confirmation or one quarter of GM expansion toward 32%+. Ceiling 2.5%, and only at ≤$74 average cost or after margin inflection.
- **Risk rules**: hard stop $70; exit on any two thesis-invalidation triggers (GM <30% ×2 quarters; backlog <$5B; 45X disallowance; DSO >140 with cash conversion <0.75x; ≥10% customer loss). Trim ⅓ at $115–120, down to 0.5% residual at $130–135.
- **Do not**: chase the +14.9% gap; hold alongside ARRY or FLNC (0.65 correlation, commoditizing category — own the leader or the challenger, not both); treat this as a quality-compounder allocation while ROIC is sliding 50.6% → 29.2%.
- **Re-underwrite**: Nov-16 Capital Markets Day (re-rating option) and Jan-26 Q3 print (gross margin is the confirmation event). Before tranche 2, ask IR: *"What is the balance of receivables sold or reclassified at 31-Mar-2026, and under what facility?"*

**Disagreement & data-gap flags**: Growth (BUY) vs Value (HOLD) vs Quant (SELL) split is about price, not business — resolved in favor of Value on entry discipline. Peer multiples were unavailable across agents (sector taxonomy returns oil majors); no 10-K full text, credit rating, or CDS data was retrievable; the Fin Risk price discrepancy was resolved in favor of $91.13. These gaps temper, but do not change, the verdict.

*Data-integrity resolution: the Fin Risk Analyst's $125.42 price and ~$19.0B market cap are an artifact of a stale price series; I verified against daily prints. All sizing below uses $91.13 / $13.92B cap / $12.87B EV. The $79.33 level is the unfilled gap reference.*

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** (structurally informative split)

The disagreement is **not** about the business. **Twelve of twelve agents agree the franchise is real, the balance sheet is a fortress, and the backlog is genuine.** Nobody alleges fraud (Short Analyst explicitly cleared it; Beneish M-Score artifact correctly diagnosed).

The split is cleanly along two axes:

**Axis 1 — Earnings momentum vs. price trend.** Growth + Alt Data + Sector (fundamentals, all bullish) sit against Quant + Value (price/valuation, both bearish). This is a *classic decoupling*, not a contradiction: the fundamentals were positive for two straight quarters while the stock fell 51%. The 2-Nov +14.9% gap is the first evidence of the price converging toward the fundamentals rather than vice versa.

**Axis 2 — Policy earnings vs. margin quality.** Geo Legal, Non-Fin Risk, and Short all converge on the same finding from three different angles: **~31–40% of gross profit / adjusted EBITDA is policy-contingent (45X + tariff recoveries), and gross margin is in a 4-quarter downtrend (35.9% → 31.1%).** That is the single most important cross-agent corroboration in this file. Three independent methodologies found the same thing independently.

**Conflict resolution — where I overrule:**
- **Value vs. Growth on price.** Value wins the *entry-timing* argument. Growth's "market implies zero growth" is a clever but fragile framing; Value's DCF ($88 base vs. $91 spot) uses explicit cash flows. There is **no margin of safety at $91.** Growth's own honest caveat concedes Rule of 40 = 35 and a ~10% Q3 guide.
- **Quant's SELL is discounted to neutral.** Its own report disclaims statistical significance (alpha t-stat ≈ −0.5), admits the revision score is a **false positive** (FY2031 vs FY2030 comparison), and concedes 65–75% of variance is idiosyncratic — which cuts both ways. A factor model that has no value signal on a name trading at 17x EV/EBITDA is not a sell signal; it is a *no-signal*.
- **Non-Fin Risk's insider selling is real but bounded.** The Short Analyst's honest caveat is decisive: his feed returned filing *metadata* only, not direction/size — and management bought back **$162M of stock in Q2 FY27**, the first meaningful repurchase. Net insider *disposition* (largely 10b5-1/RSU and a pre-IPO holder exiting) is a negative sentiment datapoint, not a thesis-breaker.
- **Macro beats Geo Legal on the discount rate; Geo Legal beats Macro on the earnings.** The 10Y at 5.13% with a *real* 2.60% is already ~42% de-rated. But the 45X/FEOC chain is the one thing that can hit volume *and* margin *and* the multiple simultaneously. **Geo Legal is the binding constraint on position size.**

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.0% starter → 2.5% max at target cost**

**Kelly logic.** Probability-weighting the agents' own scenario work:

| Scenario | Prob. | Price | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bull — energy shock makes solar the cheap power; 10Y → 4.50%; re-rate to 25x | 30% | $125 | Macro |
| Base — backlog converts, margins settle ~30–31%, 16–19x | 45% | $90 | Value |
| Bear — 10Y >5.50%, FY28 air pocket, 14x | 25% | $62 | Macro / Value |

**Expected value ≈ $94.2 vs. $91.13 spot = ~3.4% edge.** With 69% annualized volatility, a 3.4% edge is *statistically indistinguishable from zero*. Kelly at that edge with that variance produces a fraction of a percent — which is the mathematically honest answer and the reason this is a **starter, not a position.**

**Therefore:**
- **Initiate at 1.0% of portfolio.** This is a "presence + monitoring" allocation sized to the fact that twelve specialists collectively produce a coin-flip on timing. It buys the right to be right if the CMD re-rates the name, without paying for conviction I do not have.
- **Ceiling: 2.5%**, reached only at ≤$74 average cost or after gross margin inflects. Do not build toward the ceiling at $91.
- **Why not 0.5%?** Because the downside is genuinely bounded: net cash $1.04B, zero LT debt, survives a −35% revenue scenario, $6B backlog, and the Short Analyst — whose job is to find the bear case — rated it **NO EDGE**. This is not a 0.5%-or-pass risk profile.
- **Why not 3–5%?** Three independent agents flag policy-contingent earnings at ~31–40% of gross profit, gross margin is in a four-quarter downtrend, and Value's base intrinsic value is *below* the current price. High conviction, low risk → 3–5% is the wrong bucket. **This is medium conviction with elevated, binary policy risk → 1–3% bucket, entry-biased to the low end.**

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector/factor concentration — the binding portfolio issue.**
- NXT's 1Y beta to SPY is **2.65** (vendor 5Y: 1.93); annualized vol **69.4%**; max drawdown **51.1%**. A 1% NXT position contributes roughly **2.65% of market beta** — i.e., **1% of NXT ≈ 2.65% of SPY-equivalent risk**. Size it as a 2.65% beta exposure, not a 1% one.
- A 20% S&P drawdown plausibly maps to a **35–40% NXT drawdown** (Fin Risk). If the portfolio has a risk budget, this consumes ~1.3% of total-portfolio drawdown at a 1% weight. That is acceptable; at 3% it is 4% of drawdown budget in one policy-dependent name.
- **Correlation:** ARRY 0.65, FSLR 0.52, ENPH 0.44 (Quant). Moderate — roughly 55–77% diversifiable — but *these are the wrong comparables to worry about.* The real correlation risk is any existing **high-beta growth / long-duration / AI-power-thematic** sleeve. NXT is functionally a **duration + policy beta instrument**, and it will correlate with rate-sensitive growth far more than the 0.52 FSLR print suggests.
- **Do NOT hold NXT alongside ARRY or FLNC** — 0.65 correlation with the #2 tracker, in a commoditizing hardware category where Short's central finding is that ARRY is growing 37% and taking share while NXT's margins compress. Own the leader or the challenger, not both.
- **Genuine portfolio positive:** zero net debt, zero credit exposure, no refinancing cliff. This is pure equity duration — it does not add to a credit-risk or leverage factor tilt.

**Factor tilts added:** +High Beta, +Momentum *loser* (12-1 −17.1%), +Quality (ROE 25.1%, GP/Assets 0.285 — best in group), −Value (23.7x P/E vs FSLR 12.8x). Note the Quality tilt is *decaying* — ROIC 50.6% → 38.5% → 29.2% in two years. **The Quality factor exposure that justified the premium is itself in decline; do not underwrite this as a quality-compounder allocation.**

**Guidance:** cap NXT + any adjacent clean-energy/solar-equipment holdings at **5% of portfolio combined**, and cap NXT at 2.5% standalone.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale-in on thirds — do not chase the gap**

Initiating in full the session after a +14.9% gap, with the stock at its highest level since August and Value's base intrinsic value ($88) *below* spot, is poor execution. The Nov-2 move left an **unfilled gap from $79.33 to $83.41** — a natural liquidity magnet and the first re-entry zone.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 0.5% | **At market now (~$91)** | Presence only. Protects against the CMD re-rating the name without us (Growth and Alt Data both flag this risk). |
| **2** | 0.5% | **$76–80 zone** (late-Oct low $76.48; gap fill) | Where Value's 25%-discount buyers and the FCF-yield >5% cohort accumulate. |
| **3** | 1.0% | **Post-CMD confirmation** (16-Nov) *or* one quarter of gross-margin *expansion* toward 32%+ | The two conditions that would move Value's intrinsic value to $105–115 and justify paying near spot. |
| **Skip tranche 3 if** | — | CMD is vague on FY28, or GM prints below 30% | Then hold 1.0% and treat as a watchlist position. |

**Do not average down below $68** — that is Value's aggressive-buy level only *if* the margin thesis is intact; if price is there because gross margin broke 30%, the thesis is dead, not cheap.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Hard stop (price): $70.** Below the late-Oct low ($76.48) and ~23% below entry. With 69% vol, a tighter stop will be triggered by noise alone; a looser one exceeds the position's risk contribution.

**Thesis invalidation — fundamentals over price (any two of these = exit):**
1. **Gross margin <30% for two consecutive quarters.** *This is the primary kill-switch.* Fin Risk: a 500bp GM compression costs ~$178M of EBIT (26% of operating income) — more damaging than a 20% volume decline. Short Analyst's escalation trigger independently sits at exactly this level.
2. **Backlog falls below $5.0B**, or bookings show a genuine air pocket rather than a quarterly lump. Destroys the entire visibility argument.
3. **45X disallowance, clawback, or adverse FEOC interpretation.** Geo Legal's explicit downgrade-to-High trigger. Note the $312M receivable.
4. **DSO >140 days with cash conversion <0.75x**, or a 10-K disclosure that the FY26 year-end receivable reduction (~$780M, against ΔWC of only +$7.3M) came from a **factoring/true-sale facility with recourse.** This is the single most valuable open question in the entire file — **direct it at IR before tranche 2.**
5. **Loss of a ≥10% customer**, or a court ruling adverse in the GameChange matter (treble damages, TrueCapture injunction tail).
6. **Macro override:** 10Y persistently >5.50% *with* 10Y real >2.90% → cut to 0.5% regardless of fundamentals; project FIDs for 2028+ COD will defer and backlog conversion stalls.

**Trim triggers (sell discipline):**
- **$115–120:** trim one-third. This is the low end of the Street's PT range (Mizuho $101, BMO $114, Jefferies $115) and ~30% above base intrinsic value.
- **$130–135:** trim to a 0.5% residual. Street median is $126–138; do not hold a policy-beta cyclical through a full round-trip to the Street's own target.
- **On gross margin breaking 30%:** trim 50% immediately, *even if the price is down* — that is margin-quality deterioration, not a buying opportunity.

**Time/event stop:** Re-underwrite at the **16-Nov-2026 Capital Markets Day** and the **26-Jan-2027 Q3 print**. If FY28 framing at the CMD is vague on bridging the 31-Dec-2027 placed-in-service cliff, **hold at 1.0% indefinitely rather than adding.** The Jan print is the real confirmation event — Alt Data is explicit that no signal in its stack predicts a print 12 weeks out.

**Watch-items:** 7-Dec FOMC (hike is consensus-adjacent), 4-Dec Section 232 polysilicon effective date.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — 1.0% (scaled, not bought)**

**A small initiation is the correct action and a full position is not.** The synthesis is unusually clear on *why*:

- **The business is not the question.** Twelve agents, four independent methodologies, zero fraud findings, a net-cash balance sheet that survives a −35% revenue shock, a $6B backlog, and a #1 share position 2.8x the nearest pure-play rival. The **Short Analyst — the agent whose mandate was to break the thesis — returned NO EDGE** and explicitly rejected shorting it at 16x forward earnings after a 42% drawdown.
- **The price is the question.** Value's base intrinsic value ($88) sits *below* spot ($91). There is no margin of safety. Expected value (~$94) with 69% volatility is a coin flip. Buying 3% of a portfolio into a coin flip with a 51% realized max drawdown is how you lose the right to be right.
- **The earnings quality is the risk.** Three agents independently found that ~31–40% of gross profit is policy-contingent (45X + tariffs) and that gross margin has fallen four consecutive periods (35.9% → 31.1%). This is why the position is capped at **2.5%**, why the **<30% GM rule is a hard exit**, and why **Geo Legal — not Macro, not Valuation — is the sizing constraint.**

**Summary of the action:**

| Parameter | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Action** | Initiate — 1.0% starter |
| **Ceiling weight** | 2.5% (only at ≤$74 avg cost or post-GM inflection) |
| **Execution** | 0.5% now / 0.5% at $76–80 / 1.0% post-CMD confirmation |
| **Hard stop** | $70 (price) — but fundamentals override price |
| **Primary kill-switch** | Gross margin <30% for two consecutive quarters |
| **Trim** | ⅓ at $115–120; down to 0.5% at $130–135 |
| **Do not** | Chase the +14.9% gap; hold alongside ARRY/FLNC; treat as a quality-compounder allocation |
| **Pre-tranche-2 action** | Ask IR: *"What is the balance of receivables sold or reclassified at 31-Mar-2026, and under what facility?"* — an evasive answer caps the position at 1.0% permanently |

**This is a 2–3 year hold, sized as a 2.65%-beta instrument, underwritten as a policy-and-margin-sensitive cyclical — not as a compounder.** The Nov-16 CMD is the re-rating option; the 26-Jan gross-margin print is the confirmation or the exit.

# Sector Brief: Nextracker / "Nextpower" (NXT) — Solar Trackers & Utility-Scale Solar Equipment

**Data note:** FMP classifies NXT under sector "Energy" (industry "Solar"), which pulls an irrelevant peer set (XOM, CVX, SHEL). I substituted the economically correct peer group — solar equipment/tracker vendors — and flagged where estimates are mine. NXT's fiscal year ends 31 March; latest data = Q2 FY27, ended 2 Oct 2026.

---

## 1. Sector Overview

NXT competes in utility-scale solar equipment — principally single-axis trackers plus software, and increasingly storage, electrical BOS and power conversion. Global tracker demand is growing at roughly 20% p.a. (Mordor: ~$38B in 2026 → ~$96B by 2031; note published market-size estimates vary 5–9x by definition, so I weight the *growth rate*, not the level). The end-market is booming but policy-timed: US utility-scale installs hit 9.6 GWdc in Q2 2026 (+61% YoY) as developers rushed the 4 July 2026 safe-harbour deadline, taking total Q2 to 11.4 GWdc (+45%); SEIA/Wood Mackenzie still model ~44 GWdc/yr through 2031, but 2026 is roughly flat because ~30% of the early-stage pipeline is stuck in permitting. Structure is oligopolistic — NXT is the clear #1, with Array Technologies a distant #2 (ARRY's 2025 revenue is only 36% of NXT's) and Shoals a niche #3 — and barriers are real (bankability track records, wind-load engineering, warranty books, domestic-content manufacturing).

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Utility-scale demand + AI/data-centre load growth.** 43.4 GW of utility-scale solar planned for 2026 (EIA); solar+storage = 70% of H1 2026 US capacity additions. Management describes an "energy super cycle" driven by data-centre electricity demand — a genuinely new, non-subsidy demand driver.
- **~216–240 GWdc safe-harboured pipeline with a hard 31 Dec 2027 placed-in-service deadline.** This converts to contracted, near-term demand: NXT's backlog is at a record **>$6B** as of Q2 FY27 (vs >$5B a year earlier), giving unusually high revenue visibility through CY2027.
- **Content expansion and internationalisation.** Trackers are standard kit (single-axis = 86.8% of the tracker market), and NXT is layering storage, electrical BOS and power conversion onto the same project relationship — raising revenue per project. Its 100% domestic-content tracker also captures IRA domestic-content bonuses that peers cannot easily match.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Policy cliff risk.** 45Y/48E credits are phasing down, safe-harbouring closed 4 July 2026, and projects must be in service by 31 Dec 2027 or lose eligibility. That pulls 2027 demand forward and creates a plausible 2028 air pocket absent legislative extension. Permitting delays hit ~30% of early-stage projects; FEOC/foreign-entity rules add compliance cost and supply-chain constraints.
